key_insight: GradAudit uses parameter gradients to reveal whether a vision-language model was trained on specific image-text pairs, not just on individual images or text.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare AI, it offers a stronger way to audit whether sensitive medical images and reports may have been included in model training, supporting privacy and provenance checks.
method: Analyze internal gradient patterns rather than only model outputs.
Look for stable, well-aligned gradients on training samples versus noisy, inconsistent gradients on non-training samples.
Use the gradient signature to detect true cross-modal image-text exposure.
evidence_signal: Across medical and general-domain datasets, the method outperformed state-of-the-art baselines in both pretraining and fine-tuning settings, and a copyrighted-content case study showed existing methods underestimated training-data use.
watch_item: Gradient-based auditing may require internal model access and careful interpretation, so it may be harder to deploy on fully closed models or at scale.
paper_title: Revealing Training Data Exposure in Vision Language Large Models via Parameter Gradients
